methodology.pathA: [VERIFY(self): PQ verify + APPROVE, SENDER(self): send 1 wei], signatures [ARBITRARY witness]
methodology.pathB: [VERIFY(self): payer SECP256K1 check + APPROVE, SENDER(self): PQ verify + send 1 wei], signatures [ARBITRARY, SECP256K1]
methodology.budgetRule: fits(B) iff tightLimit(VERIFY gas used) + 100 (ARBITRARY intrinsic) <= B, tightLimit = used + used/63 + 2,000 rounded up to 1,000 (the 1/64 the frame keeps back across STATICCALL). Node answers override it where a node with that budget was asked: stock sidecar at 100k, BUDGET-010 sidecar (staked account) at 1M
methodology.floorCrossCheck: every receipt is compared with two formulas: the EIP-8141 text, and the devnet ethrex build's (forshtat/ethrex 9aa3645d, crates/common/types/transaction.rs), which also prices the EIP-8250 nonce calldata rlp(nonce_keys)||rlp(nonce_seq) (3 bytes = 192 gas here) and weights witness bytes 4/16 in the standard intrinsic
methodology.signingTimes: wall clock on one laptop (Apple Silicon) while the amd64-emulated devnet was running; indicative only, and the Python/C reference signers are not product signers
methodology.sameShape: every scheme is measured in the same two transactions: VERIFY(self, data 0x01) + SENDER(self, data 0x03||funder, 21 B, an internal 1-wei CALL; the frame itself carries no value), one ARBITRARY entry whose witness is the signature (ETHFALCON: signature + its 1,024-B public key, bound to a 32-B commitment in the account code). The account keeps its 32-B key words in code, reads no storage in VERIFY, and calls the verifier cold; Forge measures the same calldata with vm.cool before each call
methodology.securityColumn: upstream claims at the pinned commits (parameter tables, header comments, READMEs), quoted so rows can be compared; nothing was assessed here. 128-bit classical hash-based claims hold only up to the stated per-key signature cap; keccak256 vs SHA-256 changes gas (native opcode vs precompile 0x02), not the claimed level
